messages:
Connor O'Brien: ✅ Phase 1 paging enablement check — ready to flip on perf-canary paging for us-east-1?

Connor O'Brien: Final checklist (please add a quick :thumbsup: / notes): https://drive.redwoodinference.com/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/perf-canary-rollout-checklist

Connor O'Brien: Scope reminder: us-east-1 only, models = top-3 (per runtime list), paging only for sustained p95 regression + tokens/sec drop conditions. Warns already live.

ReleaseBot: Deploy window reminder: change freeze lifts in 30m. If approving, please confirm runbook + rollback owner.

Noah Patel: Runtime side: 👍 from me.
- Baselines for us-east-1 refreshed last night (runtime build 2026.02.02-rc3)
- Regression evaluator min samples = 80 / 10m (per tuned settings)
- Confirmed kernel tags and runtime build id in canary payload

Noah Patel: Also validated alert payload links: dashboard -> model panel -> region filter works.

Aisha Bello: SLO/toolkit wiring looks correct. Paging rules are only bound to top-models + us-east-1 label. :thumbsup:

Aisha Bello: One note: we’re using 15m sustain for page, 5m sustain for warn. That matches the doc + what we agreed post-storm.

Allison Grant: Confirmed alert formatting + dedupe keys in incident-bot handler are using:
`model_id + region + metric + runtime_build`
So a single sustained regression shouldn’t fan out multiple pages.

Allison Grant: Also confirmed runbook link is included in payload and resolves:
https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert

Rafael Mendes: On-call routing checked.
- Warning -> #eng-runtime (threaded)
- Page -> on-call rotation + #eng-oncall + #incidents

Rafael Mendes: If it goes sideways, please use the “safe-disable” toggle (don’t just kill pods). It preserves audit + avoids partial alerts. (Runbook section 2.3)

Sean Gallagher: SRE sign-off 👍
Criteria met from our side:
- dashboard has p95/p99, tokens/sec, queueing split
- paging dampening enabled
- disable switch drill done this week

Sean Gallagher: Vanessa — any fleet changes pending in us-east-1 in the next ~24h that would contaminate baseline?

Vanessa Ortiz: Fleet: no planned GPU driver roll or host image in us-east-1 until tomorrow night.
Only scheduled change is a small capacity rebalance within same SKU pool (shouldn’t move perf materially). I’ll keep an eye on it and post if anything changes.

Marissa Cole: Product OK to enable paging for phase 1. We should treat any page as “pause expansion” by default until triaged (not necessarily rollback, but no new rollouts).

Connor O'Brien: Great. I’m going to proceed unless anyone objects in next 10 mins.

Connor O'Brien: Confirming owners if page fires tonight:
- primary triage: on-call (Rafael / rotation)
- runtime escalation: Noah / kernel team if kernel tag implicated
- if suspected fleet: Vanessa

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: works for me.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup:

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup:

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup:

Noah Patel: :thumbsup: (I’m around for the next few hours.)

Connor O'Brien: Flipping it now.
Change: enable paging ruleset `perf-canary-paging-v1` for `region=us-east-1`.

ReleaseBot: Change applied: perf-canary paging enabled
- region: us-east-1
- ruleset: perf-canary-paging-v1
- effective_at: 1770049788
Audit: https://console.redwoodinference.com/audit/changes/pc-2147

Connor O'Brien: ✅ Paging enabled. Please sanity check that we see “paging rules loaded” in the canary status panel within ~5-10m.

Aisha Bello: Status panel updated: rules loaded + last eval ok. :white_check_mark:

Rafael Mendes: Incident-bot test alert came through in #incidents as expected (deduped). :white_check_mark:

Sean Gallagher: Cool. No further action. If we get a page, follow runbook and please tag me if we’re considering a release freeze.

Connor O'Brien: Closing out. Next checkpoint tomorrow: review on-call load + any false positives before expanding model coverage.
